task.issue_text: A UTF-8 .env file can raise UnicodeDecodeError on Windows when the locale codec is not UTF-8. Reading an .env file without an explicit encoding should default to UTF-8, while callers that explicitly pass another encoding must keep that behavior. Public report: https://github.com/theskumar/python-dotenv/issues/207

+++ b/dotenv_loader.py
@@ -5,13 +5,11 @@
 import locale
 from pathlib import Path
 
-DEFAULT_ENCODING: str | None = None
+DEFAULT_ENCODING: str = "utf-8"
 
 
 def read_env(path: str | Path, *, encoding: str | None = None) -> str:
     """Read one dotenv-style text file."""
 
     selected = encoding if encoding is not None else DEFAULT_ENCODING
-    if selected is None:
-        selected = locale.getpreferredencoding(False)
     return Path(path).read_text(encoding=selected)

report.root_cause: read_env used locale.getpreferredencoding() as fallback, so when the platform locale is ASCII the function tried to read a UTF-8 .env file with ASCII encoding, raising UnicodeDecodeError.
report.summary: Default to UTF-8 when no explicit encoding is provided, preserving caller‑specified encodings.
report.evidence: Test failure shows UnicodeDecodeError when locale.getpreferredencoding() returns "ascii"; updating DEFAULT_ENCODING to "utf-8" fixes the issue.
